top_strength: Dustin gave an honest, well-reasoned estimate using a clear equivalency (26-ft truck ≈ 1600–1800 sq ft home) and handled the customer's live push for extra labor transparently — explaining that a bigger crew would raise the hourly rate roughly in proportion to the time saved rather than overselling it as a bargain.
coaching_note: The customer all but announced he was price-and-speed shopping (asking to add labor to cut the timeline before he leaves town Sunday) — that was the exact moment to introduce No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee to differentiate Einstein while he decides. Instead Dustin competed on crew size and scheduling logistics alone, never got the customer's name, and let the call end on "call you back after I check with my wife" with no email, no next step, and nothing locking the lead in place.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently casual and cooperative ("gotcha," "no sweat," "appreciate you") and calm through a mid-call scheduling mix-up, but never used the customer's name once and offered no explicit empathy statements, keeping the tone friendly but task-focused rather than warm.
